reponse:
I don't know the amount — the credit terms in Orbitly's signed MSA aren't in what I could find.

What I did establish:
- The Nov 12 incident (08:47–12:27 UTC, ~3h40) caused stale dashboard data from an ingestion-service config change; all events were processed late, none lost [7].
- Jonas Pike (VP Operations) is claiming the service credit under **section 7 of their MSA**, and Sam told him he'd come back on the credit after checking terms with finance [7].
- Their MSA was **negotiated custom in 2024**, so generic 99.9%-SLA credit tiers can't be assumed. Sam couldn't find it attached to the HubSpot deal; Maya says it's in the **legal folder on the shared drive — ask Avi** [3][1].

One caveat worth flagging before settling: this incident was delayed/stale data, not full unavailability, and contracts often only count full unavailability as downtime — so section 7's definitions of "Downtime" and "Service Credit" determine whether a credit is owed at all [1][7].

Searches run: Orbitly contract/outage/SLA credits, Orbitly signed MSA service credit terms, Orbitly MSA section 7. Sources read: the incident-report email thread, #deal-desk Slack thread, and Sam's SLA-terms conversation. The next step is pulling section 7 of the signed MSA from Avi to calculate the actual figure.
